chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Nasr al-Mada'ini wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I ask you, may I be your ransom, regarding the falcon (bazi) when it catches its prey and has been named over it, then it kills the prey; is it permissible to eat it?' He (peace be upon him) wrote with his own hand and seal: 'If you named it, you eat it.' And Ali ibn Mahziyar said: 'I read it.'

key_terms.الْبَازِي: Falcon (a type of bird of prey used in hunting)
key_terms.بِخَطِّهِ وَخَاتَمِهِ: With his hand and his seal (indicating authenticity)
key_terms.سُمِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: Named over it (reciting Bismillah or naming the animal)

ai.seo_question: Is the prey caught by a named falcon permissible to eat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the condition of 'tasmiyah' (naming) for game hunted by trained birds of prey, establishing that the prey becomes halal upon death if the name was invoked, even if the hunter did not personally deliver the killing blow. The inclusion of the Imam’s handwritten and sealed response (khatuhu wa khatmuhu) underscores the authority and authenticity of this specific legal nuance within Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the practical application of Quranic hunting laws, linking the physical act of hunting with the spiritual requirement of invoking God's name.
